label: early copy step (recall 2-3) with input a/o/i/n in long sequences
explanation: Very sparse reset-gate unit (0.03% of steps, tiny magnitudes). Fires only in the copy phase, almost entirely at recall_idx 2-3 (t = 11-12), in long sequences (L=9 holds 86% of mass, L=8 13%, never L<=6), when the fed-back input token is a, o, i (and weakly n/r); it never fires in the original or delimiter phase or on other input letters/digits. Activation is somewhat higher when the token being output is also from {a,o,n,i,r} and when the input token repeats in the original sequence, but these do not sharpen precision much. The predicate captures ~95% of activation mass but precision is only ~4%: most a/o/i/n inputs at these positions do not activate it, and the deciding factor was not found in token-level variables. Small residual activity at the final step of L=9 sequences (t=17).

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: phase=2 & in_tok=o (+4.81), phase=2 & in_tok=a (+4.67), phase=2 & in_tok=i (+4.25), phase=2 & out_tok=r (+2.28), phase=2 & out_tok=o (+2.20), phase=2 & in_tok=n (+2.17). Lower it: orig8=- (-2.28), orig6=- (-1.80), to_go=2 (-1.63), to_go=1 (-1.61).
